queue.title: Waiting on you, and it is the one that holds the rest up: both ways of showing a headline number are on the Pacing tab of the build now on your screen. Say A or B and the other is deleted. Full text in docs/2026-09-06-queue-detail.md.

Your call on refreshing our frozen copies of the game's symbol files. I recommend holding until the engine team publishes a build manifest; the silent-drift fault itself is already fixed and landed.
Toy Story is silent here and I have ruled out the obvious causes, so the gap is inside our sound emulation. The next question is cheap and yours: does the OLD emulator play it with sound?

The next thing I would build, and it is owed rather than chosen: when something swaps the machine out from under a connected tool, the tool is currently never told, so it keeps reading a world that no longer exists. The contract team already adopted our request for this.

The reason I keep having to ask you to look at panels instead of reading them myself: the window can report its top bar to a connected program but not any panel. Fixing it converts a class of 'please look at this' into something I can measure.

Nothing notices if the plane picture draws the wrong tile in every cell; I transposed its lookup and all thirty-one tests stayed green. Low stakes because a scrambled picture is obvious, but the clicked reading IS guarded, so the two halves are held to different standards.

The page guiding the rest of the panel work disagrees with itself about what colour a headline number is, and I copied the wrong half onto your decision card before catching it. Fix is an appended correction, since the page's line numbers are stamped to a revision.

Our contract checks read replies only, so they are blind to every duty to REFUSE a bad request. This was a proposal for weeks; it now has a real defect it would have caught. Do not re-argue it from principles.
A nightly that reports when the contract team moves past our pinned copy, without blocking anyone. Nothing new to build; it calls a road already built.
